performance.baseline_kind: prior native-architecture frontend, not legacy Go frontend

method.static_serving: local loopback HTTP with gzip level9 for compressible assets
method.api_data: fixed synthetic fixtures shared by both variants within this run
method.readiness: visible route selector, fonts ready, fixed 1000ms settle
method.static_bytes: Resource Timing encodedBodySize of static subresources; excludes response headers and navigation HTML
method.heap: V8 usedSize after HeapProfiler.collectGarbage; not process RSS

limitations: Real production JS is rendered in Chromium; all API data is a fixed synthetic fixture. This does not validate live authentication, pricing accuracy, money operations, or backend latency.

Static transfer uses a local Node HTTP server with gzip level 9 and 300-byte Resource Timing response overhead; it is not production CDN or WAN throughput. Navigation HTML is reported separately from the static subresource total.
JS heap is V8 usedSize after CDP HeapProfiler.collectGarbage, not browser/process RSS, GPU memory, server memory, or a leak test.

Measurement occurs after the route-specific visible selector, resolved fonts, and a fixed 1000ms settle interval. Expected anonymous refresh 401 is permitted. Fresh browser contexts, disabled HTTP cache, identical viewport/locale/theme/API latency, and alternating A/B order reduce but do not eliminate timing noise. Three samples establish a small reproducible comparison, not a statistical SLA.
Any external network dependencies are replaced with an empty successful response and recorded; this intentionally excludes real third-party payloads from the controlled fixture.
A timing sample can include browser startup/order/host noise. Transfer and decoded byte counts are deterministic for the same route and bundle.

visual_review.native: Password form comes first, centered desktop composition, compact header and optional collapsed game. Desktop dark and 390px light fields, main action and labels are legible with no horizontal overflow; normal anonymous refresh removes the injected interrupted-session banner.
visual_review.legacy: Desktop uses a login column plus a prominent signal puzzle. Social providers precede password fields. The narrow page keeps that provider-first order, placing the password form lower than Native. Both legacy widths render without horizontal overflow.
visual_review.comparison_limit: Only anonymous sign-in visual/accessibility-by-inspection and basic rendering are compared. No real authentication, money, provider behavior, browser RSS, or controlled old-Go performance claim.
